# FirstComms

> FirstComms tests emergency responder radio coverage in buildings and installs the
> systems that fix it — a BDA, also called an ERRC system or public safety DAS.
> Based in Toms River, New Jersey; serving New Jersey and the surrounding states.

Contact: 732-302-8992 · https://first-comms.com/

## What an ERRC system is

Firefighters and police carry handheld radios. Concrete, steel, low-E glass and
below-grade levels block those radio signals, so a radio that works outside a
building can go dead inside it. An ERRC system (Emergency Responder Radio
Coverage) fixes that: an antenna on the roof picks up the public safety signal,
a bi-directional amplifier (BDA) boosts it, and antennas distributed through the
building carry it to every floor, stairwell and basement.

"ERRC system", "BDA", "public safety DAS" and "emergency radio coverage system"
all refer to the same thing in ordinary use.

## When a building needs one

Fire code requires adequate in-building radio coverage. The governing standards
are IFC Section 510, NFPA 1225 (which absorbed NFPA 1221), NFPA 72 for monitoring
and supervision, and UL 2524 for the equipment itself. Whether a specific building
needs a system is decided by measurement, not assumption: the building is tested
against a grid, and if it already passes, nothing needs to be installed.

Radio coverage is commonly checked before a certificate of occupancy is issued,
so a missing or failed test can delay sign-off on new construction.

This is not a new-construction-only requirement, which is a common
misunderstanding. The obligation attaches to the building, not its age. Existing
and occupied buildings are caught by it during renovations, on a change of use,
or when a fire official tests the building and it fails.

A poorly specified or badly commissioned amplifier can raise the noise floor of
the public safety network it is meant to support. This is the practical reason
jurisdictions scrutinise how these systems are specified, and the reason a
channelised (Class A) amplifier is preferred over a broadband (Class B) one
where the choice is available.

## What FirstComms does

- Emergency responder radio coverage testing (grid testing and a written report)
- ERRC / BDA system design
- Installation, by their own crew rather than subcontractors
- Final acceptance testing and certification
- Annual testing, battery replacement and record-keeping
- Repair of existing BDA systems

Not offered: permitting is not handled in house, and the company does not do
cellular or Wi-Fi distributed antenna systems. The work is emergency responder
in-building communication only.

## Pricing

Cost depends on building size, how many floors need covering and how strong the
outside signal is. A firm price before testing is a guess. Buildings that pass
the test need no system and nothing to buy.

## Service area

Headquarters: 1390 Lakewood Rd, Toms River, NJ 08755.
Serving New Jersey, New York, Pennsylvania, Delaware and Connecticut.
